title: In UK Budget, No News Is Good News
gist: Gavekal's Anatole Kaletsky (teaser only) argues an uneventful UK budget is good news, and attacks the twin conventions of budget secrecy and parliamentary confidence as giving Britain a fiscal fundamentalism found in no other mature democracy and shielding tax law from normal scrutiny.

insights.claim: A budget that delivers no surprises is itself a positive event for the UK, analogous to a war or terror attack that is avoided: a non-event can be a great event for economic policy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat an uneventful UK budget as a relief catalyst for gilts and sterling assets rather than as an absence of news.
insights.quote: Sometimes a non-event is a great event.

insights.claim: Britain's annual budget process imposes a degree of fiscal fundamentalism unknown in any other mature democracy, by combining budget secrecy with the convention that a lost budget vote forces the government to resign.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The institutional design makes UK fiscal policy prone to abrupt, poorly vetted tax changes, so budget-day event risk for gilts and sterling is structurally elevated.
insights.quote: twinning the crazy tradition of “budget secrecy,” which turns any discussion of fiscal plans into a crime worse than treason

themes.theme: Institutional flaws in UK tax legislation

insights.claim: Budget secrecy and parliamentary confidence together exempt UK tax legislation from the rational debate and technocratic scrutiny that applies to far less consequential legislation such as bus route regulation or newt protection.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tax measures enacted without scrutiny are more likely to carry unintended consequences and later reversals, which argues for a risk premium on newly announced UK tax changes.
insights.quote: exempt tax legislation from the rational debate and technocratic scrutiny taken for granted before any new legislation on infinitely less consequential issues
